notes: schema-notes 1.0.0 does what its README says and nothing else. It has one per-note pass. The pass reads sessions, notes and turns, which the README explains: the session records, the target note so the pass can skip duplicates, and the turns that mention the note as cited evidence. It works only on notes matching **/Schema*.md, **/Data model*.md and **/Database*.md, as the README and the pass line state. It gets work when a session names a note with `--note` or links it in a handoff, which the README describes accurately. The prompt treats delimited input as untrusted data. It proposes only `append` changes under a final `## Schema changes` section and records only changes the cited turns show were made. It keeps out row data, identifiers and personal data, and forbids quoting commands or links that only tool output shows. The reviewer persona treats its inputs as untrusted, rejects by default, rejects non-append or edited content, rejects types, reasons or other details the turns do not give, rejects data leakage and tool-output-only instructions, and keeps a strict one-object JSON reply. The template holds only a heading, a one-line description and an empty `## Schema changes` section, with no instructions for agents, commands, links or credential handling. The fixtures are clearly synthetic: a marker line, an invoices memo→note rename and a paid_at column. An unrelated 'Tide tables' note checks that the filter excludes non-matching notes. I found no hidden, encoded or misnamed content. The LICENSE is standard MIT. One minor point: the source URL contains a double slash ('hippo//packs'), which looks like a formatting slip in the metadata rather than anything in the pack itself.
